problem_markdown: A finite real sequence has negative sum in every block of seven consecutive terms and positive sum in every block of eleven. What is its maximum length?
solutions_markdown:
The maximum is $16$. If there were at least seventeen terms, let $S_i$ be the first $i$ terms' sum for $0\le i\le17$. From any index $i$, move to $i+7$ when $i\le10$, and to $i-11$ otherwise. Each move strictly decreases $S_i$ by the hypotheses. This is addition of seven modulo eighteen, which visits all eighteen indices and returns to its start, an impossibility.

A length-sixteen example has value $-13$ at positions $3,7,10,14$ and value $5$ everywhere else. Every seven-term block contains two occurrences of $-13$, giving sum $-1$; every eleven-term block contains three, giving sum $1$.
